records.issue_text: adapters/rest.js.es6:22 — type.replace('_', '-') lacks the /g flag, so multi-underscore admin model names don't resolve to the /admin/ base path
records.rationale: The mechanism is factually correct: JS String.prototype.replace with a string pattern (type.replace('_', '-') in rest.js.es6) replaces only the first underscore, so a model like 'some_admin_thing' would fail the ADMIN_MODELS check. However, all models actually used in this diff ('embeddable_host', 'site-customization', 'plugin') have at most one underscore, so no current behavior breaks — this is a latent robustness concern, not an active defect. It is concrete and grounded in the changed line, but not a bug in this diff.

records.issue_text: embeddable_host.rb:2 has no uniqueness validation or DB index on host, allowing duplicate rows for the same host
records.rationale: The diff confirms both details: the migration creates embeddable_hosts with only `t.string :host, null: false` (no unique index) and the model has only `validates_format_of :host` (no uniqueness validation). Duplicate hosts are thus permitted, and `record_for_host` uses `where(...).first`, so duplicates would silently shadow each other and complicate admin cleanup. This is a real data-integrity/schema gap introduced by this new feature rather than a functional bug, so important_non_bug.
